amends: docs/annotation-protocol.md section 3.4 (new); step 3 of the batch workflow in docs/main-dataset-protocol.md
batch_01_note: Batch 01 was frozen before this feature existed and was labelled by live browsing; it is reported that way.
blank_rule: a capture of 8192 bytes or less is flagged suspect whether or not it repeats; rendered 1365x1000 pages in these batches run 250-290 KB median
invariants: The snapshot panel exposes availability, state, byte size and duplicate count only. No risk score, risk level, evidence code, stratum, or coordinator-key field reaches the form.
A capture is addressable only through a sample_id present in that annotator sheet, and the route requires the annotation token.
The unit of annotation stays the registrable domain as a visitor meets it; blank, shared, or missing captures must be opened live or recorded as a failed load under section 3.3.
Labels remain human-produced. The crawler image is a display of the page, not a verdict.
prepared_by: assistant; tooling only. The assistant supplies no labels and reads no label authorship.
reason: The annotator can review a page but cannot review several hundred sites one live tab at a time at acceptable cost. The captured viewport is the same page the assessment was built from, so it shortens the assessment-to-annotation distance rather than widening it.
reporting: The paper states the share of labels made from captures versus live browsing, and that a viewport screenshot under-covers pages whose intent appears only below the fold, in forms, or on deeper paths.
summary: Labels may be produced from the page the crawler captured for the queued URL, shown inside the blinded labeling form, instead of opening every domain in a live tab.
verification: tests/test_snapshot_labeling.py asserts no decision field or screenshot path appears in the sheet payload and that captures are only reachable through assigned sample_ids.
